evidence.name: Find Zeroes of a Polynomial Algebraically
method_steps: Set the polynomial p(x) equal to zero (p(x) = 0).
Identify the type of polynomial (linear, quadratic, etc.).
If linear, solve the resulting linear equation for x.

State the value(s) of x as the zeroes of the polynomial.

evidence.name: Verify Relationship between Zeroes and Coefficients of a Polynomial
method_steps: Identify the polynomial and its coefficients (a, b, c, etc.).
Determine the zeroes of the polynomial (if not given, find them algebraically).
Calculate the sum(s) of the zeroes (e.g., α+β for quadratic, α+β+γ for cubic).
Calculate the product(s) of the zeroes (e.g., αβ for quadratic, αβγ for cubic, and sums of products taken two at a time for cubic).
Apply Vieta's formulas using the coefficients to find the theoretical sum(s) and product(s) (e.g., -b/a, c/a for quadratic).
Compare the values calculated from the zeroes (steps 3 & 4) with the theoretical values from Vieta's formulas (step 5) to verify the relationship.

State the resulting quadratic polynomial.

evidence.name: Calculate length using tangent-radius property and Pythagorean theorem
method_steps: Identify the given information: radius (OP) and distance from the center to the external point (OQ).
Recall the property that the radius to the point of tangency (OP) is perpendicular to the tangent (PQ).
Recognize that the points O, P, and Q form a right-angled triangle (ΔOPQ) with the right angle at P.
Identify the hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle, which is the side opposite the right angle (OQ).
Apply the Pythagorean theorem: OP² + PQ² = OQ².
Substitute the known values and solve the equation for the unknown length (PQ).

evidence.name: Geometric construction of lines (tangent, secant) parallel to a given line
method_steps: Draw the given circle and the specified given line.
Draw a line perpendicular to the given line, ensuring it passes through the center of the circle.
Identify the two points where this perpendicular line intersects the circle. These are potential points of contact for tangents parallel to the given line.
At one of these intersection points on the circle, construct a line perpendicular to the radius at that point. This newly constructed line will be a tangent parallel to the given line.

To draw a secant parallel to the given line: Draw another line parallel to the given line, making sure it passes through the interior of the circle. This line will intersect the circle at two distinct points, thus being a secant.
